_meta.note: Canonical schema for .planning/config.json. Source of truth for keys, types, enums, and defaults. Validated by bin/config.mjs; the cad-config workflow catalog is derived from this. `src` is CONFIG-LAYER SCOPE, not enum provenance: [repo] = settable in either layer; [global] = the user-global layer only, and a repo layer setting it is stripped at the merge and named in the read face's warnings (bin/lib/global-only-keys.mjs, cross-checked against this field by self-verify in both directions); absent = repo-settable. `repo_only` is a DIFFERENT and much narrower marker than `src`, and the two are read separately: present and `true` means only that repository's own .planning/config.json can set the key, so bin/config.mjs REFUSES a write aimed at the user-global layer at write time rather than stripping it at the merge; absent means either layer, which is every other key. The test it encodes, for a maintainer deciding whether a new key qualifies: would a user-global value AUTHORIZE a change to a repository that never opted in? If yes the key is `repo_only`; a key that merely has a sensible per-repo value is not.
_meta.types: bool | int | string | string_or_null | enum | array_string | array_enum. int accepts an optional 'min'. enum/array_enum carry 'values'. `grammar` is an OPTIONAL further narrowing of a value whose type already passed, naming one predicate in bin/config.mjs's frozen GRAMMARS registry: the type says what kind of value this is, the grammar says which of those values this key serves. It is evaluated at the write face (set/check) and over a whole file (validate), a null value skips it because null means the question was never asked, and a marker naming a predicate the registry does not hold is an error rather than a silent pass - a key claiming a grammar nothing enforces is the failure the marker exists to prevent.

granularity.purpose: How many phases the roadmap gets - new-project roadmap step only (coarse 3-5 / standard 5-8 / fine 8-12 phases); it splits no phase into tasks

stakes.purpose: What a break in this project costs - the question routing asks, rather than what a dispatch costs. solo = nobody else runs this, a break costs only my time; shipped = other people run this, a break comes back as a bug report; critical = a break is not a bug report. It is a FLOOR and not the level every phase pays: a dispatch resolves at or above it, never below, and the phase's own declared PLAN `files:` read at resolve time are what raise it. UNSET floors at `solo` when every plan in scope was read clean, and at the `shipped` default when any of them could not be - a plan Cadence cannot read holds the configured level rather than dropping under it

workflow.inline_plan_threshold.purpose: Task count at/below which a plan runs inline vs its own doc

workflow.max_plan_tasks.purpose: Task ceiling PER PLAN, not per phase - a phase needing more capacity gets MORE PLANS, sequential where they share files, and `## PHASE TOO BIG` is returned only when no number of plans of that size can deliver the phase, which is a statement about the PHASE's scope and not about task count. The ceiling the planner is given up front, so an oversized plan is split rather than silently built. Re-decided 2026-08-17 against both of its forces and landing on 8, unchanged: cold-prefix cost - `weight.mjs resident` puts the executor's fixed dispatch prefix at 12,488 bytes, about 2% of a measured executor dispatch, so what an extra plan re-buys is the cold pass over the plan and the phase's artifacts rather than the prefix - and context risk - 15 executor checkpoints of 21 on this repo's `.planning/trace.jsonl`, every one of them from a plan already under this ceiling. design-notes/dd-plan-task-ceiling.md carries the dated arithmetic

workflow.max_plan_bytes.purpose: Byte ceiling on what a SINGLE plan's `files:` frontmatter declares, measured as the sum of the on-disk sizes of those declared paths - PER PLAN and not per phase, the same reading workflow.max_plan_tasks carries, so a plan over it is split into MORE PLANS rather than shrunk in place. Those declared paths are what an executor dispatch is handed, and on one measured PLAN-1.md they were about 90% of a 70,554-token dispatch while nothing measured them against anything. A crossing is REPORTED and nothing is refused: plan-size report only (`bin/planning.mjs`), which workflows/plan.md hands the resolved value at its `check_size` step as `plan-size --max-bytes`; no dispatch path, agent frontmatter key or spawn seam consults it, so an over-ceiling plan is still planned and still executed. That is planning.max_capture_bullets's disposition and for its reason - the user may have authorized the full scope one step earlier, and a check that refused what they just authorized would be arguing with them. The default is the 75th percentile of the declared-byte distribution over this repository's 43 archived plans rounded UP to the next 25,000 (p25 207,298, p50 401,107, p75 667,580, p90 933,283, max 1,282,083, measured 2026-08-26; it fires on 10 of the 43), which is the derivation rule the six workflow.max_dispatch_tokens.* keys already state; references/config-reach.md carries the reach row

workflow.max_dispatch_tokens.cad-planner.purpose: Token ceiling on ONE the planner dispatch's live context window, read off the `tokens` figure that dispatch's terminal lifecycle event left on .planning/trace.jsonl - a FINAL-WINDOW PROXY, not a sum across the dispatch's turns. A crossing is REPORTED and nothing is refused: trace window report only (`bin/planning.mjs`), which reads the record after the dispatch has already returned, and no dispatch path, agent frontmatter key or spawn seam consults it. The default is this role's 75th-percentile terminal figure on this repo's own record rounded UP to the next 25,000 (n=28, p75 188,135, max 247,585, measured 2026-08-17); references/seam-spawn-agent.md carries the argument and references/config-reach.md the reach row

workflow.test_command.purpose: Command Cadence runs to test (null = none). Honoured from the user-global config layer only: a `.planning/config.json` setting it is stripped at the merge and named in the read face's warnings, so a config that arrived with a clone cannot choose what Cadence runs - set it with `config.mjs set --global`

workflow.lint_command.purpose: Command an executor runs for static analysis before it commits (null = none set, so planning.mjs detect-commands reads the project's own manifests instead). LINT ONLY - there is no companion typecheck key; the detected arm covers both. Honoured from the user-global config layer only: a `.planning/config.json` setting it is stripped at the merge and named in the read face's warnings, so a config that arrived with a clone cannot choose what Cadence runs - set it with `config.mjs set --global`

parallelization.enabled.purpose: Run independent plans concurrently. On by default; false is the intentional opt-out. Engages only when the plans are provably independent AND the host's worktree.baseRef is "head" - choose_path falls back to sequential otherwise, so the default is safe on a host that cannot honour it

parallelization.use_worktrees.purpose: Isolate parallel writes in git worktrees

git.protected_branches.purpose: Branches Cadence won't commit to directly

git.on_protected.purpose: What to do on a protected branch (DESIGN §5, git rails)

git.integration_branch.purpose: Two-tier branch model: 'milestone' creates a per-milestone integration branch as the branch worktrees merge back into (where they fork FROM is the host's worktree.baseRef setting); 'trunk' creates no integration branch and commits land on the base governed by on_protected

git.auto_branch.purpose: How the integration branch is created at cycle start: 'ask' prompts once, 'auto' creates/switches silently, 'off' stays put

git.base_branch.purpose: Branch new work branches off (null = current)

git.create_tag.purpose: Cut the release tag at land - on the pulled base, after the merge confirms (tag-after-merge). It governs that tag cut and nothing else: no other step reads it, and a manifest bump never depends on it

git.on_land_cleanup.purpose: After a successful land/merge, return to the base branch, pull, and reap the merged integration branch

git.issue_check.purpose: Read-only issue-tracker report at the start of a land: which issues this branch's commits reference and which of them are still open on the forge this repository CONFIGURED - git.forge_provider and git.forge_repo, never a host detected from the origin URL - degrading to one line when it cannot be read, including the line that names which forge keys are unset. It reports only - nothing on this path ever writes to a tracker

git.forge_provider.purpose: Which forge hosts this repository's issue tracker, resolved ONCE at project setup by /cad-new-project or /cad-adopt and read at land time in place of any host detection: bin/issue-check.mjs picks its provider row from this value rather than classifying the origin URL, so a repository that temporarily loses its remote does not silently change behaviour. Spelled with the same vocabulary bin/lib/issue-decision.mjs's HOST_TABLE uses for its rows. null means unasked - the setup step has not run or the user has not picked a provider yet. Settable in either config layer: naming which forge you use is a preference, and it authorizes nothing on a repository that never named ITSELF - binding a call to a repository is git.forge_repo's job, and that key is repo_only.

git.forge_repo.purpose: The owner/name slug this repository's forge calls address, resolved ONCE at project setup - offered as a default read off origin, confirmed by the user - and read at land time in place of any host detection, as bin/issue-check.mjs's --repo selector. null means unasked. repo_only: a user-global slug would point EVERY repository's forge calls at one target, which is exactly the authorization test _meta.note states, so only that repository's own .planning/config.json may set it.

git.forge_host.purpose: The Forgejo instance host the user confirmed at setup, spelled `hostname` or `hostname:port` when the instance is not on its scheme's default port - the port a browser reaches the instance on, never an SSH port - resolved ONCE at project setup and read at land time in place of any host detection, where bin/issue-check.mjs turns it into the tea login NAME the call is made under. NEVER derived from the origin URL: on a split SSH endpoint the origin's host is the SSH hostname, not the instance the user reaches in a browser, which is the shape this repository itself has - so it is ASKED outright and confirmed. null on the github and gitlab providers, whose hosts are fixed, and null anywhere else means unasked. Settable in either config layer, for the same reason git.forge_provider is: naming which instance you work with is a preference and authorizes nothing on a repository that never named itself.

git.auto_close.purpose: Opt-in end-to-end close: cad-milestone/cad-land run audit -> tag -> PR -> merge -> reset with no per-step prompts, halting on a surviving blocker/high risk_surface finding. ONE key, TWO resolutions, and they are allowed to disagree. AUTHORIZED is honoured repo config layer only for the unattended publish, and for the GitLab MR create that publishes the branch itself: that close mutates ONE repository, so only that repository's own .planning/config.json can authorize it and a user-global value authorizes nothing on any host (D-08; git-publish.mjs publish and authorized, both through lib/repo-auto-close.mjs). REQUESTED is the MERGED value, read on purpose - cad-land skips the publish ask on it and the land gate reads that same merged value, so the gate's blocker/high halt is what replaces the human it switched off, and both must read one value. Setting it globally therefore skips the ask and still refuses, naming which authorization was missing.

planning.max_capture_bullets.purpose: Bound on the SUBSTANTIVE walked bullets .planning/CAPTURE.md may hold - the Todos, Seeds and Notes count with the `- None.` placeholder excluded, which is what `planning.mjs capture-check` reports. A crossing is REPORTED and nothing is refused, the same consequence workflow.max_dispatch_tokens.* carries and for the same reason: capture-check report only (`bin/planning.mjs`), no writer consults it, so /cad-capture and /cad-execute's open items keep filing at a queue that is over. The default is this repository's own live figure rounded up - 30 substantive walked bullets measured 2026-08-25 after the hand sweep - so the bound sits ABOVE a healthy tree and fires on GROWTH rather than on arrival, because a bound that reddens the day it ships teaches its reader to ignore it. What it is for: the hand sweep took this queue to zero on 2026-08-08 and it regrew to 276 walked items in sixteen days, because nothing measured it against anything. references/config-reach.md carries the reach row

memory.backend.purpose: Where notes/observations route: 'builtin' runs zero-dep BM25 recall over .planning/, 'none' disables recall

review.key_file.purpose: Path override for the provider key env file (never a key). Honoured from the user-global config layer only: a `.planning/config.json` setting it is stripped at the merge and named in the read face's warnings, so a config that arrived with a clone cannot choose where a provider key is read from - set it with `config.mjs set --global`

review.request_timeout_ms.purpose: ms before a review provider HTTPS request is aborted (a high-effort review can take minutes); 600000 is the execution-host ceiling

review.max_prompt_tokens.purpose: Estimated-token ceiling (chars/4) on a review or consult payload; an over-cap payload is refused with ok:false, reason over-cap before any request is issued; cross-model provider calls only - the free claude-subagent reviewer never runs that script

review.providers.openai.tiers.balanced.purpose: OpenAI model id for the balanced tier

review.providers.openai.tiers.cheap.purpose: OpenAI model id for the cheap tier

review.providers.deepseek.tiers.cheap.purpose: DeepSeek model id for the cheap tier

review.triggers.plan.gate.purpose: How the plan review gates. Leave it UNSET and the stakes level decides - advisory at solo, blocking at shipped, adjudicated at critical; writing any value pins it at every level and warns

review.triggers.plan.tier.purpose: Model tier for plan review - cross-model reviewers only; the claude-subagent reviewer's model comes from the routing cell. Leave it UNSET and the stakes level decides - cheap at solo, balanced at shipped, flagship at critical; writing any value pins it at every level

review.triggers.plan.effort.purpose: Reasoning effort for plan review - cross-model reviewers only; the claude-subagent reviewer's effort is frontmatter-frozen. Leave it UNSET and the stakes level decides - low at solo, medium at shipped, high at critical; writing any value pins it at every level

review.triggers.diff.gate.purpose: How the diff review gates. Leave it UNSET and the stakes level decides - off at solo, off at shipped, blocking at critical; writing any value pins it at every level and warns

review.triggers.diff.tier.purpose: Model tier for diff review - cross-model reviewers only; the claude-subagent reviewer's model comes from the routing cell. Leave it UNSET and the stakes level decides - cheap at solo, cheap at shipped, balanced at critical; writing any value pins it at every level

review.triggers.diff.effort.purpose: Reasoning effort for diff review - cross-model reviewers only; the claude-subagent reviewer's effort is frontmatter-frozen. Leave it UNSET and the stakes level decides - minimal at solo, low at shipped, medium at critical; writing any value pins it at every level

review.triggers.risk_surface.gate.purpose: How the risk-surface review gates. Leave it UNSET and the stakes level decides - blocking at solo, blocking at shipped, blocking at critical, because the trigger fires only on a detection match and there is no level at which a matched risk surface is worth waving through; writing any value pins it at every level and warns

review.triggers.risk_surface.tier.purpose: Model tier for risk-surface review - cross-model reviewers only; the claude-subagent reviewer's model comes from the routing cell. Leave it UNSET and the stakes level decides - cheap at solo, balanced at shipped, flagship at critical; writing any value pins it at every level

review.triggers.risk_surface.effort.purpose: Reasoning effort for risk-surface review - cross-model reviewers only; the claude-subagent reviewer's effort is frontmatter-frozen. Leave it UNSET and the stakes level decides - low at solo, medium at shipped, high at critical; writing any value pins it at every level

review.triggers.risk_surface.surfaces.purpose: Which of the eight risk surfaces the risk-surface review fires on - a heuristic match in a category outside this list does NOT fire the trigger. Left unset it means all eight, and it is also the UNANSWERED state: the first risk_surface fire on a project that has not answered runs the structural scan and asks once, then writes the answer here. There is deliberately no default array - a default of all eight would make "the user chose everything" indistinguishable from "nobody has answered"

review.triggers.risk_surface.waive_routi.purpose: Which surfaces may NOT raise this project's plan-time ROUTING floor. It waives a LEVEL, never a review: the blocking risk_surface review still fires on the actual diff, and this key cannot turn it off. Naming a surface here is the one way to route below the computed floor - the raise is withheld and the level holds at the configured `stakes`, never below it, and every waiver applied is named in the resolve's `reason` with the surface and the file it would have raised on. A surface that is NOT named still raises: waiving `secrets` on a phase that also touches `destructive` routes at the raise. Left unset it waives nothing, which is a different state from an empty answer for the same reason its `surfaces` sibling has no default array

review.triggers.phase_diff.gate.purpose: Aggregate review of the merged phase diff after parallel execution (per-plan reviews never see cross-plan interactions). Leave it UNSET and the stakes level decides - off at solo, off at shipped, adjudicated at critical; writing any value pins it at every level and warns

review.triggers.phase_diff.tier.purpose: Model tier for the merged-phase review - cross-model reviewers only; the claude-subagent reviewer's model comes from the routing cell. Leave it UNSET and the stakes level decides - cheap at solo, balanced at shipped, flagship at critical; writing any value pins it at every level

review.triggers.phase_diff.effort.purpose: Reasoning effort for the merged-phase review - cross-model reviewers only; the claude-subagent reviewer's effort is frontmatter-frozen. Leave it UNSET and the stakes level decides - low at solo, medium at shipped, high at critical; writing any value pins it at every level

review.consult.enabled.purpose: Allow a second-model consult at dead-ends

review.consult.attempt_threshold.purpose: Failed fix attempts (or red-test iterations) on one bug before cad-debug offers a consult

review.decision_review.tier.purpose: Model tier for /cad-decision-review's refute-then-adjudicate pass - cross-model reviewers only; its claude-subagent arm is cad-reviewer at the session default and resolves no model at all

review.decision_review.effort.purpose: Reasoning effort for /cad-decision-review - cross-model reviewers only; the claude-subagent reviewer's effort is frontmatter-frozen
